flawed_step: 0037 (with the same defect propagating through 0040 and 0043; the auxiliary domain slip at 0029 is noted separately)
counterexample:
Take L_1 = L_2 = (P({a,b}), \subseteq), the power set of a two-element set ordered by inclusion. This is a complete lattice with join = union and meet = intersection; being the topology of the discrete two-point space (equivalently a finite Boolean algebra), it satisfies the frame distributivity law, so it is a frame. Let phi = id : P({a,b}) -> P({a,b}). The identity preserves arbitrary unions and finite intersections, so it is a frame homomorphism. Then S_3 = phi[S_1] = P({a,b}) and \preceq_3 = \subseteq, so every hypothesis of the corollary (and of line 0029, A \subseteq S_3) is satisfied.

Choose A = { {a}, {b} } (a subset of S_3, and also of S_1).

Left side of the chain (lines 0033-0034): phi(\bigvee_1 A) = \bigvee_1 A = {a} \cup {b} = {a,b}.

Right side asserted by line 0037: \bigwedge_2 phi[A] = \bigwedge_2 { {a}, {b} } = {a} \cap {b} = \emptyset.

So line 0037 asserts {a,b} = \emptyset, which is false. The step is not an instance of the definition of frame homomorphism: that definition gives phi(\bigvee_1 A) = \bigvee_2 phi[A] = {a,b}, a join, not the meet \bigwedge_2 phi[A] written in the proof. Lines 0040 and 0043 carry the same wrong operator (\bigwedge_3 phi[A] = {a} \cap {b} = \emptyset, still not {a,b}), and line 0041 cites Lemma 1, a statement about suprema lying in S_3, to justify an equality between infima, so it does not support the step either. Consequently the chain ends at \bigwedge_3 phi\restriction[A] = \emptyset while the quantity needed for the conclusion drawn at line 0050 is \bigvee_3 phi\restriction[A] = {a,b}; the displayed computation therefore never establishes arbitrary join preservation.
reasoning_summary:
Steps 0001-0015 merely quote Lemma 1 (the supremum in L_2 of any T \subseteq S_3 lies in S_3) and Lemma 2 (the infimum in L_2 of any finite F \subseteq S_3 lies in S_3) from the parent theorem; as cited external lemmas they are admissible. Lines 0017-0025 restate the definition of frame homomorphism (finite meet preserving and arbitrary join preserving) correctly.

The join-preservation section begins at 0029 with 'Let A \subseteq S_3'. This is already a domain slip: the map under test has domain S_1, and the very next line forms \bigvee_1 A and phi[A], both of which require A \subseteq S_1. Since S_3 \subseteq S_2 need not meet S_1 at all, the expression at 0033 is in general ill-formed, and even when it is formed the argument covers only subsets of S_3 rather than all subsets of S_1. I did not stop here, because on its own this reads as a recoverable transcription error and it is invisible in cases where S_1 = S_2 = S_3.

I stopped at line 0037. Starting from phi(\bigvee_1 A), the proof asserts equality with \bigwedge_2 phi[A], citing the definition of frame homomorphism. That definition yields the join \bigvee_2 phi[A], not the meet, and the substituted claim is false: with L_1 = L_2 = P({a,b}), phi = id, A = {{a},{b}}, the left side is {a,b} and the asserted right side is \emptyset. The error is not cosmetic, since it propagates: line 0040 keeps the meet and justifies it by Lemma 1, which is a statement about suprema and hence cannot license an equality of infima, and line 0043 ends the chain at \bigwedge_3 phi\restriction[A]. The conclusion drawn at line 0050 ('arbitrary join preserving') therefore does not follow from anything the chain establishes; in the counterexample the chain computes \emptyset while join preservation requires {a,b}. Note also that the 'where' clause at 0048 declares \bigvee_1, \bigvee_2, \bigvee_3 as the suprema, confirming that the \bigwedge symbols in 0037-0043 are not an alternative notation for joins but genuinely the wrong operation, and leaving \bigvee_2, \bigvee_3 declared yet never used.

For completeness (not required for the verdict): the finite-meet section 0055-0076 uses the right operator throughout and its appeal to Lemma 2 at 0066 is apt, but it repeats the domain slip, quantifying over F \subseteq S_3 instead of F \subseteq S_1. So even the second half establishes the property only on subsets of S_3, and line 0079 ('the result follows') is unsupported.
